name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+16 district with strong Democratic fundamentals
Castro's incumbency and large fundraising edge
model.rationale: San Antonio's TX-20 leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Joaquin Castro out-raised his little-known challenger by more than ten to one. With no competitive polling or outside spending, fundamentals point to a comfortable Castro win.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a major outside spending push for the challenger could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that voted Democratic by a wide margin in recent cycles. He enters the general election with the advantages of incumbency, name recognition, and a large financial edge, having raised over half a million dollars while Republican Edgardo Rafael Baez has raised under fifty thousand.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Castro's chances around 95 percent. The district's partisan lean and the challenger's minimal resources make an upset highly unlikely, and the forecast expects Castro to win comfortably.
